text_summary.body: He plants the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he comes to his end, and no one helps him.

setting.period: End of Antiochus IV's reign (164 BC)
setting.body: Antiochus went east in 166/165 to raise funds; after failing to plunder a sanctuary of Artemis in Elymaïs he died at Tabae in Persia, "smitten with madness, as some say" (Polybius 31.9). News reached Babylon in Kislimu 148 SE (BM 35603). 1 Macc 6 adds that he heard of the Jews' victories; 2 Macc 9 tells the story with legendary additions (Driver).

competing_reconstructions.label: Death after the rededication
proponents: 1 Maccabees 6:7 (he hears that the abomination has been pulled down)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Death in Persia after news of the Temple's recovery.

competing_reconstructions.label: Death before the rededication
competing_reconstructions.summary: The death (ch. 9) precedes the cleansing (10:1–8); a letter of year 148 refers to the late king. Not modelled as a constraint because the sources disagree (claim under review).

not_applicable.commentary: Interpretive commentary is recorded on the Daniel 11 prophecy records.
